title: Curves and genus
statement:
Let $k$ be a field (in this chapter algebraically closed). A *curve*
over $k$ is a separated scheme of finite type over $k$ of dimension
$\le1$; it is *smooth* (resp. *proper*) if its structure morphism is
smooth (resp. proper). A *connected curve* is a nonempty
connected curve of dimension exactly $1$ (so $\Spec k$ is a curve but
not a connected curve).
For $C$ smooth proper connected, the
*genus* of $C$ is $g=\dim_{k}H^0(C,\Omega^1_{C/k})$ (invariant
under algebraically closed extension of $k$).

proof.text: For an extension $k\subseteq k'$ of algebraically closed fields and a smooth proper connected curve $C/k$, apply [lem-sc-genus-invariant] to this curve and extension. Its displayed equality is $g(C_{k'})=g(C)$. These are the genera of [def-sc-genus], whose statement explicitly identifies genus with $\dim H^0(\Omega^1)$. Extracting this equality, and discarding the additional Jacobian compatibility, proves the extension-invariance parenthetical.

source.place: Final parenthetical: invariant under algebraically closed extension of k; implemented by the existing lem-sc-genus-invariant equality clause.

proof_origin.place: Genus-invariance parenthetical: direct extraction from the existing stronger lemma lem-sc-genus-invariant.
